function: Channel estimation: CNNs map the received pilot signal to the direct channel (CDCE) and the cascaded BS-IRS-device channel (CCCE) in an active-IRS-aided uplink (p. 6-7).
system: Uplink; single-antenna IoT device, BS with K antennas, active IRS (reflection-type amplifiers) with N elements; Rayleigh links; carrier frequency not stated (p. 3, 9).
method: Supervised CNNs: CDCE (three conv, three max pooling, one linear) and CCCE (six conv, three pooling, one linear), trained on LS-estimate labels with AdamW, 200 epochs (p. 6-9).
data_channel: Own simulator: Rayleigh fading and own path-loss model (PL0 = -30 dB); 10000 samples split 90/10 for training and validation, 5000 regenerated test samples (p. 3, 9).
test_conditions: Test set of 5000 regenerated samples, no other scenario stated (p. 9); MSE versus SNR (p. 10) and versus K, N = 128 (p. 11).
baselines: Non-learned LS and MMSE estimators for the direct and cascaded channels; no earlier learned estimator is compared (p. 10).
metrics: MSE in dB of the direct and cascaded channel estimates versus SNR and K; Sum-MSE for the power allocation; training and validation loss (p. 9-11).
complexity: Order of complexity: CDCE O(48384KN + 4K^2N) (p. 8), CCCE O(14400KN + 2K^2N^2) (p. 9); parameter counts per layer in Tables I and II (p. 7-8).
q1_support: p. 3: "and active IRS to BS are all Rayleigh fading channels"; the path loss is its own model with PL0 = -30 dB (p. 9). No 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO, QuaDRiGa, or measured data is mentioned.
q2_support: p. 9: "we regenerate the 5000 samples used to appraise the performance of the proposed CDCE / CCCE network". Only SNR (Fig. 11, p. 10) and K (Fig. 12, p. 11) are swept; no transfer, fine-tuning, or unseen scenario is reported.
q3_support: p. 10: "the proposed CDCE network outperforms convention LS and MMSE schemes in estimating DCs". Only LS and MMSE are compared (Figs. 11-12); no earlier learned estimator or other network is a baseline.
q4_support: p. 8: "the total computational complexity of the proposed CDCE network is" O(48384KN + 4K^2N); p. 9 gives O(14400KN + 2K^2N^2) for CCCE.
q5_support: p. 9: "Assuming 10000 samples are collected at BS" is its own simulated data; no code or data link is given and no public dataset is used.
notes: Area 2 (channel estimation). The learned parts are the CNN estimators CDCE and CCCE (p. 6-7); the optimal power allocation factor is closed form (p. 5), not learned. Training labels are the LS estimates, not the true channels: "the conventional LS CE scheme can be employed to acquire the label hLS" (p. 6). PDF title: Power Optimization and Deep Learning for Channel Estimation of Active IRS-Aided IoT, arXiv preprint 2407.09254v2 (p. 1); the DOI is not printed, so the match rests on the file name.
